In this molecule:
- The carbons at positions 1, 2, 4, and 5 are part of double bonds
- The carbons at positions 3 and 6 are not part of double bonds

For carbon atoms:
- Those involved in double bonds (positions 1, 2, 4, and 5) would typically have sp² hybridization
- Those only involved in single bonds (positions 3 and 6) would typically have sp³ hybridization

The question asks for the "most common" hybridization of carbon atoms in this molecule. Since 4 out of 6 carbon atoms (those at positions 1, 2, 4, and 5) have sp² hybridization, while only 2 out of 6 (those at positions 3 and 6) have sp³ hybridization, the most common hybridization is sp².
